annoyed.instructions: A user sent this message to an AI coding assistant (markup and code blocks have been stripped). Assess how annoyed or frustrated the user appears. Evaluate wording and tone alone (all-caps, profanity, 'again', 'why did you', 'stop', 'wtf', visible exasperation), rather than how hard the task is. Straightforward directives or questions count as neutral.

target.instructions: When the user appears annoyed, who or what is that annoyance directed at?

criteria.assistant: the AI's own conduct during this session: actions it took, code it wrote, things it ignored or repeated, slow progress, or misunderstandings (including replies to its output like 'wtf', 'no', 'stop', 'again', 'why did you')
criteria.other: build tooling, external libraries or services, existing code or tests, the user's own earlier design, other people, or general product/UX remarks about the software under development
criteria.none: not annoyed: a straightforward question, command, design thought, or casual remark
